title: Cantilever Bending of Murine Femoral Necks
protocol: Obtain µCT scans of representative samples.
Scan representative samples on a µCT scanner with settings: 55 kV, 145 µA for 300 ms integration times and resolution of 10.5 µm voxels.
Ensure the captured region covers the proximal end of the femur through to the midshaft.
Analyze the µCT scans.
Obtain a 2D rendering of the anterior view of the proximal femur from representative set of µCT scans.
Compile slices with resolution of 10.5 µm voxels from the midshaft to the proximal end of the femur into a 3D rendering using software.
Determine a threshold to distinguish bone from surrounding tissue and apply a Gaussian filter for noise reduction.
Orient the 3D renderings to eliminate off-axis tilt.
Ensure that the femur's anterior surface is viewed.
Export this 2D view as an image file (.jpg or .png).
Measure the femoral shaft angle using image analysis software by drawing a line perpendicular to the femoral shaft 7 mm distally.
Draw a second line through the peak of the greater trochanter to the midpoint of the aforementioned perpendicular line.
Along the 7 mm distal perpendicular line, measure the femoral shaft diameter below the third trochanter.
Using a 3D printer, print the guides.
Harvest the mouse femurs by making a transverse incision entirely around the mouse abdomen.
Remove the tissue from the incision to the ankles.
Locate the hip socket and carefully dislocate the hip using fine forceps.
Cut additional soft tissue to remove the leg from the mouse.
Use a scalpel to dislocate and cut through the knee joint.
Clean the femurs of all soft tissue using forceps, scalpels, and paper towels.
Test harvested samples immediately or store them at -20 °C for up to 6 months.
If frozen samples are used, allow them to come to room temperature and hydrate in PBS for 2 h before prepping.
Cut tubing sections ½" to 1" in length using ¼" x ¼" square aluminum tubing.
Label each aluminum segment with the sample IDs using an etching tool.
Fill half of the tubing segments with putty.
Place these tubing segments into a fixture to hold them upright.
Place cleaned femurs into the 3D printed guides, placing the samples flat on the benchtop so the anterior surface is facing up.
Position the guide directly below the third trochanter where the shaft diameter becomes more consistent.
Hold the proximal and distal ends of the femur with one hand when applying the guides.
Firmly press the femur onto the workbench.
Place the 3D printed guide on the midshaft of the femur using your other hand.
Apply the appropriate diameter guide gently to avoid snapping the midshaft of the femur.
Place the femurs with guides in front of the corresponding aluminum segments.
Fill the aluminum segments with bone cement until just full, leaving a little room for displacement.
Place the femurs with guides on into the correct aluminum segment.
Allow the hardening agent to set completely.
Once set, place the samples in a Petri dish with room temperature phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Allow the samples to rehydrate for 2 h.
Attach and calibrate a load cell with resolution <1 N on a mechanical testing system (MTS).
Mount the load cell on the stage or actuator of the MTS when possible.
Attach a fixture with a square slot that will firmly hold aluminum segments with samples.
Secure set screws to the two sides of the holding fixture to firmly hold samples in place.
Attach a loading platen to the actuator, which can be a tapered screw with a flattened tip.
Place a stereomicroscope on a table or surface directly in front of the MTS.
Set up the mechanical testing system with a 1 kN load cell and black biaxial stage for proper sample positioning.
Attach the 3D printed mounting fixture to the load cell using an M10 threaded rod and two M4 bolts.
Position the aluminum pot securely on the mounting fixture.
View the sample through the stereo microscope equipped with a tapered loading fixture.
Save the new protocol.
Return to the main screen of the software program.
Obtain an X-ray image of the samples in the aluminum pots.
Capture the anterior view of the samples for verification measurements of potting angle.
Place the aluminum segment with sample into the holding fixture.
Tighten set screws.
Lower actuator/loading platen until it is within a few millimeters of the femoral head.
Adjust the biaxial stage to align the position of the femoral head directly underneath the loading platen using the stereomicroscope.
Lock biaxial stage in place.
Zero the position of the actuator in the MTS software.
Balance the load cell using the soft keys added in step 4.3.
Begin the loading protocol.
Capture an anterior X-ray of the sample after testing.
Export force and displacement data into graphing and calculation software.
Plot the load vs. displacement for each sample.
Fit a linear approximation to the linear segment of the load-displacement curve.
Calculate the stiffness from the slope of the linear fit.
Calculate maximum load, maximum displacement, yield load, displacement at yield point, energy to maximum load, and energy to yield point.
